clinicalPearls: An acute severe cutaneous adverse reaction with rapid onset of numerous small sterile non-follicular pustules on an oedematous erythematous base
It typically begins in the flexures and face and spreads within hours to days, with fever and neutrophilia
Most cases are drug-induced, classically by antibiotics such as beta-lactams and macrolides, with a short latency
It resolves rapidly with characteristic superficial desquamation once the culprit drug is stopped
The main differential is generalised pustular psoriasis, and histology helps distinguish them
Management is withdrawal of the culprit drug and supportive skin care; it has a good prognosis
reference.pathophysiology: Acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis is a T-cell-mediated delayed hypersensitivity reaction, usually to a drug. Drug-specific T cells and neutrophil-recruiting cytokines drive an intense neutrophilic inflammation of the upper dermis and epidermis, producing sterile subcorneal and intraepidermal pustules. The rapid onset after exposure and swift resolution on withdrawal reflect this immune mechanism, and the sterile pustules distinguish it from infective pustular eruptions.
additionalDifferentials: Pustular drug eruptions of other type
DRESS or other severe cutaneous adverse reaction
additionalInvestigations: Detailed drug history focusing on recently started agents
Skin biopsy to distinguish from pustular psoriasis
Documentation of the culprit drug and avoidance
redFlags: Extensive skin involvement or mucosal involvement
Features suggesting overlap with other severe cutaneous adverse reactions
reference.prognosis: The prognosis is generally excellent, with resolution within one to two weeks of stopping the culprit drug, though it is a severe cutaneous adverse reaction requiring recognition and drug avoidance.
pitfalls: Mistaking it for generalised pustular psoriasis and mismanaging
Failing to identify and stop the culprit drug
Treating the sterile pustules as infection
Overlooking a personal history of the same reaction on re-exposure
